feature_results.rationale: Devin's Enterprise API documentation describes a dedicated Audit Logs endpoint returning structured, per-event entries (audit_log_id, action, org_id, user_id/user_email, created_at) covering enterprise-admin actions (e.g. member/role changes, join requests, AI-guardrail violations), plus separate Enterprise API usage-metrics endpoints (sessions, searches, PR counts, and daily/weekly/monthly active-user time series) gated behind an enterprise admin API key. Cognition's Enterprise product page corroborates 'audit logs and fine-grained access controls' as a stated Enterprise capability. This is an admin-accessible, per-event audit log plus a usage-metrics API/report, satisfying the has_criteria; access is restricted to the Enterprise API tier.

evidence.excerpt: audit_log_id, action, org_id, user_id, user_email, created_at; documented actions include add_enterprise_member, update_enterprise_hypervisor_settings, search_query, ai_guardrail_violation, create_join_request, automatic_join_event
provides usage metrics including session count, search count, and PR counts for enterprises within specified time periods. Access requires an enterprise admin personal API key.
Devin Enterprise offers SOC 2 Type 2 compliance, audit logs and fine-grained access controls, and integration with custom identity providers (IdP).

constraints.description: Audit log and usage-metrics endpoints sit under the Enterprise API surface and require an enterprise admin personal API key; not documented for individual or Team-plan access.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents a dedicated PR/MR review workflow, 'Devin Review', that analyzes a diff and produces categorized review comments and suggested fixes, rather than relying only on ad hoc chat requests. This meets the has_criteria (automatically reviewing a diff/PR and producing comments or suggestions) and goes beyond the partial_criteria boundary since it integrates directly with GitHub and GitLab hosting platforms rather than being limited to local diffs.

evidence.excerpt: Devin checks for bugs and labels them by confidence level. Devin posts bugs (likely errors or incorrect behavior) as PR comments. Additionally, Devin posts security vulnerabilities and hardening suggestions as PR comments.
When Devin Review finds bugs and Auto-Fix is enabled, it will generate suggested fixes that you can review and apply directly from the diff view.

constraints.description: Devin Review operates on pull requests / merge requests hosted on GitHub (including GitHub Enterprise Server/Cloud) or GitLab (including Self-Managed GitLab); it requires the repository to be connected through one of these hosting integrations rather than reviewing arbitrary local diffs.

queries: docs.devin.ai code review PR review Devin
"docs.devin.ai" "Devin Review" GitHub GitLab pull request comments

feature_results.rationale: Devin supports instruction-driven refactors at two levels. In Devin Desktop's editor, the 'Refactor' code lens invokes the Command feature with a dropdown of pre-populated natural-language refactor instructions, or a custom instruction, applied to the selected function/class. Separately, the autonomous cloud Devin agent is documented as performing multi-file and repository-scale refactors and migrations (e.g. upgrading a library across dozens of files, converting a codebase from CommonJS to ESM, framework/legacy-language migrations) driven by a single natural-language instruction, well beyond single-symbol renames. Together these satisfy the has_criteria (refactor spanning more than one edit location, instruction-driven).

evidence.excerpt: When you click Refactor, Devin Desktop will prompt you with a dropdown of selectable, pre-populated instructions that you can choose from. You can also write your own instructions.

Migration or large refactoring tasks are often fantastic projects for Devin: after investing a small, fixed cost to teach Devin how to approach sub-tasks, Devin can go and complete the migration autonomously.

constraints.description: The single-click 'Refactor' code lens is scoped to Devin Desktop's editor (Command feature) and typically edits the selected function/class in place; multi-file, repository-wide refactors and migrations are performed by the autonomous cloud Devin agent rather than the Desktop code-lens shortcut.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's official documentation includes a dedicated 'Testing & Refactoring' use-case section and a Code Coverage tutorial describing on-request generation of unit tests targeting existing functions/files and closing coverage gaps, which matches the has_criteria directly (test code targeting specified functions/files on request) rather than being an incidental byproduct of general code generation.

evidence.excerpt: Devin can analyze your codebase's test suite and write additional tests to increase code coverage for your team.
Devin is able to read the existing file, determine what test cases you might want to implement based on the functionality that exists, and then actually write the new tests without any intervention.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents an explicit autonomous 'Agent mode' - reached after an interactive planning phase in which Devin researches the codebase and proposes a plan the user can adjust - in which it independently writes code, runs commands, browses the web, and completes multi-step tasks end-to-end without per-step confirmation, then reports back (e.g. via a pull request). This is documented consistently for both the original cloud Devin agent and Devin Desktop/CLI, satisfying the has_criteria of decomposing and autonomously executing a task with a completion report.

evidence.excerpt: Agent mode is Devin's full autonomous mode where it can write code, run commands, browse the web, and complete complex tasks end-to-end.
Devin will interpret your prompt and rapidly search your codebase to find relevant files and code snippets, and when helpful, will use this context to propose a detailed plan that you can adjust.
Devin is an autonomous AI software engineer that can write, run and test code.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents several officially supported ways to run tasks asynchronously in the background while the user does other work: the cloud Devin agent runs each session in its own isolated VM that keeps working after the user disconnects; the Devin CLI/Desktop '/handoff' command explicitly transfers a local session to an ephemeral cloud VM for long background execution; Automations start new (or message existing, long-running) Devin sessions from external triggers such as Slack, GitHub, Linear, or schedules without an active user session; and Subagents can run in a background mode where the parent agent keeps working and is notified automatically on completion. Together these satisfy the has_criteria of starting a task that continues without occupying the user's active session, with completion notification.

evidence.excerpt: When a local task demands high compute power, runs into complex dependency issues, or requires long background execution, you can transfer your local session to the cloud.
Automations let you wire external events — Slack messages, GitHub webhooks, Linear ticket updates, schedules, and custom webhooks — to Devin sessions that start automatically.
Background: Runs in parallel while the parent agent continues working. The parent is automatically notified when the subagent completes.

constraints.description: Handing off a local session for long background execution requires the Devin CLI's built-in '/handoff' command (or the open-source Devin Handoff plugin when working from another coding agent) plus access to Devin's cloud environment; it is not available as a purely local-only capability.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Desktop's documented Context Awareness engine indexes the entire local codebase (not just open files) and retrieves relevant code via a retrieval-augmented-generation approach; a specialized 'Fast Context' subagent and 'Ask Devin' natural-language search return ranked, relevant code across the whole repository. This matches the has_criteria (a natural-language query returns relevant code locations across the repository, ranked by relevance) rather than the partial_criteria (search limited to the open file/folder) or a plain-text/substring search exclusion. DeepWiki (already in the source registry) additionally provides semantic, context-grounded Q&A over an indexed repository.

evidence.excerpt: Devin Desktop indexes your codebase and uses LLMs to perform retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on your codebase... The entire local codebase is then indexed (including files that are not open), and relevant code snippets are sourced by Devin Desktop's retrieval engine as you write code, ask questions, or invoke commands.
Fast Context is a specialized subagent in Devin Desktop that retrieves relevant code from your codebase up to 20x faster than traditional agentic search.
Ask Devin's advanced code search capabilities, combined with DeepWiki, produce detailed and accurate answers grounded in your code.

constraints.description: This whole-codebase indexing/retrieval mechanism is documented under the Devin Desktop product line (the June 2026 rebrand of the former Windsurf editor), under docs.devin.ai/desktop/context-awareness/*, rather than as a feature of the original cloud-based autonomous Devin agent.

feature_results.rationale: docs.devin.ai/admin/security documents a concrete customer-facing 'Data Controls' settings page: paid-plan customers can opt out at any time, which stops data being used for training and enables Zero Data Retention with Devin's model providers. Teams-plan opt-out is restricted to administrators, and Enterprise customers receive a stronger contractual commitment that Cognition will never train on their data without express prior written consent. This is a concrete, actionable control rather than generic privacy-policy language, satisfying the has_criteria; the control is documented for paid plans generally (not enterprise-only), with Enterprise given an additional consent guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: If you're on a paid plan, you can opt out at any time on the Data Controls settings page. After you opt out, your data will not be used for training and Zero Data Retention will be enabled with our model providers.
If you are an Enterprise customer, Cognition will never train on your data without your express prior written consent.

constraints.description: Opt-out is documented for 'paid plan' customers; on the Teams plan only an administrator can exercise the opt-out. The documentation does not describe this control for a free/trial tier, and by default (absent opt-out) Devin may use data for model training.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Desktop presents AI-generated edits as inline 'diff zones' - highlighted regions in the editor showing exactly what changed, with accept/reject controls per hunk - before changes take effect, and Command generations can additionally be accepted, rejected, or given follow-up instructions via a code lens or keyboard shortcuts. Devin Review complements this at the pull-request level by organizing larger diffs hunk-by-hunk for review. This meets the has_criteria of a reviewable diff with accept/reject controls prior to writing changes to disk, at per-hunk granularity.

evidence.excerpt: Devin Desktop displays diff zones — inline highlighted regions in the editor that show exactly what changed, with accept and reject controls for each hunk.
You can accept, reject, or follow-up a generation by clicking the corresponding code lens above the generated diff, or by using the appropriate shortcuts (Alt+A, Alt+R, and Alt+F, respectively).

constraints.description: Per-hunk diff zones are the default for agent edits in Devin Desktop but can be disabled in Devin Settings -> User Interface -> Agent Diff Zones for non-Cascade agents; when disabled, those agents' edits are applied directly to the file and only a simple dismiss button is shown instead of accept/reject controls.

feature_results.rationale: Devin Enterprise documentation describes SSO via both SAML 2.0 and OIDC, with dedicated setup guides including provider-specific guides for Okta and Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), plus a two-level custom-roles/RBAC system (organization-level and account-level roles) that enterprise admins can define and assign directly, or map automatically from IdP groups delivered via SAML/OIDC claims at login. This satisfies the has_criteria (SSO via SAML/OIDC plus role/permission management for an enterprise plan); the capability is documented only within the Devin Enterprise section of the docs.

evidence.excerpt: supports both OIDC and SAML 2.0 for Single Sign-On integration, with dedicated setup guides available for both protocols

Enterprise administrators can create custom roles with specific permissions and assign them to users or IdP groups... implements a two-level role system with differentiated scopes and capabilities: organization-level roles and account-level roles

Groups are defined in the IdP's directory, and group memberships flow to Devin via SAML/OIDC claims at login time; setup guides are provided for Okta, Azure AD, generic SAML 2.0, and generic OIDC providers

constraints.description: SSO and custom-roles/RBAC are documented exclusively under the Devin Enterprise section of the docs and enterprise API; not present in individual or Team-plan documentation.

It is powered by an in-house model optimized for low-latency completions. This satisfies the has_criteria of ghost-text/inline suggestions generated while typing.

feature_results.rationale: Both sub-capabilities named in the feature definition are officially documented for Devin. (1) Duplication filter: an official devin.ai blog page ('Code Suggestion Attribution') documents automated filters that block code suggestions matching non-permissively-licensed or unlicensed public code by default, with an opt-in control to also filter suggestions matching permissively-licensed public code; enterprise customers additionally get an audit log of matches. This page is inherited from the pre-rebrand Windsurf/Codeium code-completion engine now shipped as Devin Desktop's autocomplete and still uses legacy 'Codeium' product wording, but it remains live on the current official devin.ai domain and was not previously in the discovered source registry. (2) IP indemnification: Cognition's official Platform Terms of Service state that Cognition will defend and indemnify customers against third-party claims that the Services infringe or misappropriate a third party's patent, copyright, or trade secret, with this indemnification section applying to Paid Service Tier customers and not to the Free Service Tier. Because a concrete, customer-facing duplication filter AND a stated IP indemnification commitment for paid plans are both documented, this satisfies has_criteria (either limb alone would already qualify).

evidence.excerpt: Codeium has automated filters for both non-permissively licensed and unlicensed code, meaning such suggestions will not be shown, as well as an opt-in for permissively licensed code.

Cognition shall defend Customer against third party claims that the Services infringe or misappropriate such third party's patent, copyright, or trade secret, and will indemnify and hold harmless Customer against damages and costs awarded or agreed in settlement. This section applies only to Customers on the Paid Service Tiers and does not apply to Customers on the Free Service Tier.

constraints.description: The IP indemnification commitment in Cognition's Platform Terms of Service applies only to customers on Paid Service Tiers; Free Service Tier customers are explicitly excluded.

The configurable opt-in filter for permissively-licensed matches, plus a per-match audit log, is documented as an enterprise-customer capability, distinct from the always-on default block of non-permissively-licensed/unlicensed matches.

The duplication/attribution-filter page is carried over from the pre-rebrand Windsurf/Codeium code-completion product and still refers to 'Codeium' rather than 'Devin' or 'Devin Desktop'; it should be re-confirmed against current Devin Desktop settings/documentation once a page-fetch tool is available.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's documentation states explicit repository-scale handling mechanisms: local whole-codebase indexing for individual use, a server-side 'Remote Indexing' service that indexes and embeds remote repositories (GitHub/GitLab/BitBucket) across a team without storing code locally, and a models page documenting context-window characteristics and expanded context lengths for higher plan tiers. This matches has_criteria (a documented context window or repository-scale handling mechanism such as chunking, retrieval, or extended-context models). The multi-repository / remote scale of this mechanism is documented specifically for Teams and Enterprise plans, which is recorded as a plan constraint rather than a reason to downgrade to partial, since the underlying mechanism itself is documented for the product line as a whole.

evidence.excerpt: Remote Indexing allows you to index remote repositories from GitHub, GitLab, and BitBucket for enterprise teams without storing code locally... Organizations on Teams and Enterprise plans can use Devin Desktop's Indexing Service to globally import all the relevant repositories.
For Pro users, Devin Desktop offers expanded context lengths, increased indexing limits, and higher limits on custom context and pinned context items.

constraints.description: Remote/multi-repository indexing (team-wide, cross-repo context) is documented as available to Teams and Enterprise plans; expanded context lengths and increased indexing limits are documented for Pro-tier accounts. Base/individual plans get local single-repository indexing.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a first-class, supported extensibility mechanism: the CLI docs describe connecting external MCP tool servers (stdio, SSE, HTTP transports) so their tools become available to the agent, and a dedicated MCP marketplace is documented offering one-click connections to thousands of third-party tools and services (e.g. Linear, Notion, AWS).

evidence.excerpt: MCP lets you connect external tool servers to Devin CLI, giving the agent access to APIs, databases, issue trackers, and any other service you can wrap in an MCP server.
Devin offers access to thousands of tools and integrations from a dedicated MCP marketplace, allowing you to connect to services like Linear, Notion, AWS services, and many more with a single click.

constraints.description: MCP documentation is organized separately for the Devin CLI, the chat/work-with-devin surface, and the Desktop (Cascade) product; exact transport/marketplace availability may vary slightly by surface.

feature_results.rationale: Devin's cloud/web product documents an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) experience at app.devin.ai, including an iOS Safari 'Add to Home Screen' path so that opened Devin links launch directly in the installed app; this gives mobile access to the assistant itself, not just account/billing pages. However, this is a PWA wrapper of the existing web app rather than a dedicated native iOS/Android application distributed through the App Store or Google Play, and the separately-branded Devin Desktop editor (formerly Windsurf) ships desktop-only builds for macOS, Windows, and Linux with no mobile build at all. Third-party apps calling themselves 'Devin AI' exist on app stores but are unaffiliated with Cognition and were excluded as non-official.

evidence.excerpt: Devin can now be installed as a Progressive Web App on desktop and mobile. On Chrome or Edge, open app.devin.ai and click the install icon in the address bar (or Menu → Install Devin); on iOS Safari, tap Share → Add to Home Screen.

constraints.description: The PWA install path applies to the cloud/web Devin product (app.devin.ai). The separately-branded Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) has no mobile build; its official downloads are desktop-only (macOS, Windows, Linux).

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents two complementary, officially supported delegation mechanisms across its product lines. For the cloud Devin agent, 'Managed Devins' let one Devin session act as a coordinator that scopes work, delegates pieces to multiple child Devin sessions each running in its own isolated VM, monitors progress, resolves conflicts, and compiles results - documented on docs.devin.ai and announced on Cognition's own blog. For Devin CLI/Desktop, 'Subagents' let the main agent spawn independent worker agents (foreground or background) that share tools and codebase context with the parent but keep their own separate conversation history. Both satisfy the has_criteria of documented, supported delegation to sub-agents/parallel agent instances.

evidence.excerpt: The main Devin session acts as a coordinator: it scopes the work, assigns each piece to a managed Devin, monitors progress, resolves any conflicts, and compiles the results.
Managed Devins introduced true orchestration: one Devin session acts as a coordinator, breaking large tasks into pieces and delegating to child sessions that each run in their own isolated VM.
A subagent shares tools and codebase context with the parent, but operates in its own conversation chain — it does not inherit the parent's conversation history.

constraints.description: The Devin CLI/Desktop Subagents feature is exposed behind a 'Subagents (Preview)' toggle in Devin settings per the Devin for Terminal changelog, indicating it is still in preview rather than fully generally available, distinct from the already-general-availability 'Managed Devins' orchestration on the cloud Devin agent.

feature_results.rationale: Both product lines under Cognition's current devin.ai/docs.devin.ai structure document coordinated multi-file changes from a single instruction. The cloud/autonomous Devin agent's own use-cases documentation names multi-file refactoring and new-feature building as core strengths, and the Devin Desktop local agent (Devin Local, the successor to the retired Cascade agent as of 2026-07-01) is documented as planning, executing, and verifying changes across multiple files in one operation, with subagent support for parallel sub-tasks. This meets the has_criteria bar of coordinated edits/new files across more than one file from a single instruction.

evidence.excerpt: multi-file refactoring and building new features are areas where Devin excels
Devin Local plans, executes and verifies changes across multiple files, with subagent support.

constraints.description: Devin Desktop's local multi-file agent transitioned from the legacy Cascade agent (retired 2026-07-01) to Devin Local, which is being rolled out as the current default local agent; feature coverage described here reflects the current Devin Local agent rather than the retired Cascade agent.

feature_results.rationale: Beyond the standalone Devin Desktop editor (formerly Windsurf), Cognition officially documents 'Windsurf Plugins' (the retained Codeium/Windsurf plugin lineage) as vendor-supported AI coding assistance plugins for JetBrains IDEs, VS Code, Visual Studio, Vim, NeoVim, Jupyter, and Chrome, each with documented installation steps and version requirements — clearing the two-or-more-IDE bar for officially supported multi-IDE/editor access.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents two complementary persistent-instruction mechanisms that are automatically applied without re-entering them each session. (1) 'Knowledge' (Settings & Library > Knowledge) is a store of tips, advice, facts and instructions that Devin recalls across sessions using an attached trigger description, and can be pinned globally or to specific repos so it is retrieved automatically. (2) 'Rules & AGENTS.md' for Devin CLI/Desktop are markdown rule files (preferred location .devin/rules/, with .windsurf/rules/ and the legacy single .windsurfrules file kept as fallbacks after the June 2026 Windsurf-to-Devin-Desktop rebrand) that are injected into the agent's context at the start of every session and shared via the project's own repository. Both mechanisms match the taxonomy's has_criteria of a documented rules/instructions or memory mechanism that persists guidance across sessions automatically. Devin Desktop's own FAQ notes a caveat, recorded as a constraint below: a fresh Desktop session does not retain free-form conversational memory by itself; only the separate Knowledge store and rule files persist automatically.

Rules are persistent instructions that shape how Devin CLI behaves in your project. They're injected into the agent's context at the start of every session, ensuring consistent behavior across your team.

feature_results.rationale: Devin documents an isolated/sandboxed execution model as a first-party design across every current surface, not as a plan-gated add-on. Devin Cloud provisions a dedicated per-session virtual machine (the "Devbox"/cloud sandbox) with its own file system, processes, network access, and credentials, torn down at session end. Devin Local and the standalone Devin CLI ("Devin for Terminal") enforce OS-level sandboxing (bubblewrap/socat on Linux, macOS Seatbelt, WSL2 on Windows) that restricts file and network access to explicitly granted permission scopes, and the CLI's --sandbox flag will refuse to start rather than run unsandboxed if isolation cannot be established. Devin Desktop and Devin's introductory documentation likewise describe the agent operating inside a secure sandboxed environment alongside its terminal, editor, and browser. This satisfies the has_criteria (vendor documentation of isolated execution) and goes beyond the exclusion (unisolated local shell execution).

evidence.excerpt: The Devbox is a secure virtual environment where Devin executes code, connects to resources, and interacts with your systems.
Devin operates inside a secure sandboxed environment with a terminal, a code editor, and a browser.
The --sandbox flag runs the CLI with OS-level isolation, enforcing the active Read and Write permission scopes at the operating-system level and optionally restricting network traffic.
Devin Local runs inside OS-level containers using bubblewrap and socat on Linux, macOS Seatbelt, or WSL 2 on Windows, executing compilers and runtime environments independently.

constraints.description: Windows does not currently support OS-level sandboxing for the Devin CLI; if sandbox resolution fails on a given platform, the CLI refuses to start rather than running unsandboxed.

Enterprise deployment options (e.g. Customer Dedicated Deployment / Outposts) let a customer host the sandbox/Devbox on their own infrastructure instead of Cognition's multi-tenant cloud, shifting isolation and operational responsibility to the customer.

feature_results.rationale: Devin executes shell/terminal commands directly as a core, documented capability across all current surfaces (the Cloud/Desktop agent, Devin Local, and the standalone Devin CLI/"Devin for Terminal"), with an explicit, configurable confirmation model rather than manual copy/paste. In the CLI's default "normal" mode the agent halts and displays the proposed command before every shell execution, requiring an explicit y/n approval; "Accept Edits"/"Bypass" modes and the --sandbox "Autonomous" mode relax or remove that per-command prompt (bounded by OS-level scope limits in the sandboxed case). Devin Desktop exposes four selectable "auto-execution levels" plus command allow/deny lists governing the same behavior, and Devin for Terminal additionally supports an inline `!<command>` bash mode to run shell commands ad hoc within a session, with output streamed back into the conversation. This meets the has_criteria (documented, supported command execution with usable output) rather than the partial/exclusion case of merely suggesting text.

In the default normal mode, the CLI halts whenever Devin attempts to run a shell command or write a file, displaying the proposed command, and you must press y or n to continue.

Devin Desktop provides four distinct auto-execution levels for controlling how Cascade runs terminal commands, and you can select your preferred auto-execution level via the Devin Settings panel.
